review_notes: I read the whole file and its injective counterpart. I checked the simp attributes on the add/sub/neg/zero/smul family and on the extMk lemmas. I left add_extMk, sub_extMk, neg_extMk and smul_extMk without a simp annotation on purpose, because they take hypotheses hf that aren't determined by the left-hand side. I did not run Lean, so I can't say how simps! interacts with the explicit simp lemmas. The Injective/Ext.lean file has the same smul pattern.

lemma extEquivCohomologyClass_symm_smul
    {R₀ : Type*} [Ring R₀] [Linear R₀ C] (r : R₀)
findings.problem: The simp lemmas for `extEquivCohomologyClass` cover the additive operations in both directions. For add, sub, neg and zero there is a `_symm_` lemma and a forward lemma (`extEquivCohomologyClass_add`, `_sub`, `_neg`, `_zero`). For scalar multiplication only the `symm` direction exists. A term `R.extEquivCohomologyClass (r • x)` with `x : Ext X Y n` has no simp lemma. The only forward `smul` information is in the `@[simps!]` lemmas of `extLinearEquivCohomologyClass`, and those are stated for that linear equiv, not for the plain `extEquivCohomologyClass`. In a grep of Mathlib I found no `extEquivCohomologyClass_smul`. So simp normalizes `r • x` correctly in one direction but gets stuck in the other.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma extEquivCohomologyClass_smul {R₀ : Type*} [Ring R₀] [Linear R₀ C] (r : R₀) (x : Ext X Y n) : R.extEquivCohomologyClass (r • x) = r • R.extEquivCohomologyClass x`. The proof can go through `Equiv.symm_apply_eq` and `extEquivCohomologyClass_symm_smul`. The injective-resolution file has the same gap and could get the same fix.
findings.benefit: Simp can then push `extEquivCohomologyClass` through `r • x` as it already does through `+`, `-`, `-x` and `0`. Users no longer have to rewrite by hand or go through `extLinearEquivCohomologyClass`.
